findings.summary: Test test_search_traces_raises_for_v3_format does not verify V3 exception behavior — the V3 artifact mock returns {'spans': []} so Span.from_dict never processes V3-format span data, and there is no pytest.raises assertion despite the test name
findings.failure_scenario: If _get_trace_id_if_v3_format were broken (e.g. missing base64 import, logic error, or encode_trace_id regression), this test would still pass because empty spans never trigger the detection. A regression in V3 format detection would ship unnoticed.

findings.summary: Bare `except Exception: pass` in _get_trace_id_if_v3_format swallows all exception types including MemoryError and unexpected failures from encode_trace_id or int.from_bytes
findings.failure_scenario: If encode_trace_id raises an unexpected ValueError for an edge-case OTEL trace_id (e.g. an integer that format_trace_id cannot format), the exception is silently caught, the function returns None, and the V3-format span falls through to V2 parsing which produces a generic 'Failed to create a Span object' error instead of the informative 'upgrade to MLflow 3.x' message. The user gets a cryptic error and no upgrade guidance.

findings.summary: Databricks get_trace_info RPC is executed inside download_trace_extra_fields before the `if not include_spans` early-return guard, causing an unnecessary per-trace API call when include_spans=False
findings.failure_scenario: On Databricks, a caller using search_traces(include_spans=False) for 100 traces will make 100 get_trace_info RPCs that the old code (which bypassed download_trace_extra_fields entirely when include_spans was False) never made. Each call adds latency and load with no benefit since the downloaded assessments are discarded when the function returns an empty TraceData.
